body: A Lockheed Martin F-35B has released an MBDA Meteor beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile test asset from its internal weapons bay for the first time, marking another step toward integrating the European weapon on British and Italian Lightning II fleets. The trial took place on October 7, 2026, at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, according to the F-35 Joint Program Office (JPO). The JPO and MBDA announced news of the test on November 5, 2026.

The test was a jettison, not a live missile firing. According to the JPO, the weapon test asset separated from the aircraft without igniting its rocket motor or activating its control surfaces. Such trials are designed to verify that a missile can leave an aircraft safely, either during normal operations or in an emergency, without striking the fuselage, damaging wing structures or affecting the aircraft's flight dynamics. Both organizations declared that the test had demonstrated safe separation in the complex aerodynamic environment around the F-35B's internal weapons bay. The data collected will be used to refine digital models that predict how the missile will behave during release. A combined UK/US F-35 Integrated Test Force (ITF) team, including Royal Navy, Royal Air Force and Lockheed Martin personnel, prepared and loaded the test asset, and a Royal Navy test pilot assigned to the UK's Air and Space Warfare Centre and embedded in the ITF flew the sortie.

According to MBDA, further release trials are due to take place over the coming months to verify safe separation under different flight conditions, and the campaign will eventually move to live firings. Neither MBDA nor the JPO has provided dates for those tests. The trial follows the first flights of an inert Meteor aboard a US Marine Corps F-35B from Patuxent River, announced by the Royal Air Force in February 2025. Work has also progressed on the F-35A: on December 3, 2025, Lockheed Martin announced that ground vibration testing and fit checks had been completed at Edwards Air Force Base, California. The UK leads Meteor integration on the F-35B, while Italy sponsors the F-35A effort. Despite the progress, Meteor is still several years away from entering service on the F-35: in a written parliamentary answer on April 20, 2026, UK Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard confirmed that the estimated timeline still points towards the early 2030s.
en.summary: A Lockheed Martin F-35B has released an MBDA Meteor missile test asset from its internal weapons bay for the first time, in a jettison trial at Naval Air Station Patuxent River on October 7, 2026.
en.title: F-35B releases Meteor missile from internal weapons bay for first time

body: 一架洛克希德馬丁F-35B首度自內置彈艙釋放MBDA流星超視距空對空飛彈測試體，朝英國與義大利閃電II機隊整合這款歐洲武器邁出一步。根據F-35聯合計畫辦公室說法，試驗於2026年10月7日在馬里蘭州帕圖森河海軍航空站進行，聯合計畫辦公室與MBDA於11月5日公布消息。

這次試驗屬於拋放測試，並非實彈射擊：飛彈測試體在未點燃火箭發動機、未啟動控制面的情況下與飛機分離。這類試驗旨在驗證飛彈在正常操作或緊急情況下都能安全離機，不撞擊機身、不損傷機翼結構、不影響飛行特性。兩家機構表示，試驗已證明飛彈能在F-35B內置彈艙周圍複雜的氣動環境中安全分離，蒐集的數據將用於精進預測飛彈釋放行為的數位模型。英美聯合F-35整合測試部隊團隊（包括皇家海軍、皇家空軍與洛克希德馬丁人員）負責準備與裝載測試體，由派駐英國空天作戰中心、編入整合測試部隊的皇家海軍試飛員執行這次飛行。

MBDA表示，未來幾個月將進行更多不同飛行條件下的釋放試驗，最終進入實彈射擊階段，測試飛彈分離與釋放後的飛行性能，但雙方未提供具體時程。這次試驗延續2025年2月皇家空軍公布的美國海軍陸戰隊F-35B搭載惰性流星飛彈首飛，蒐集環境數據但未釋放飛彈。F-35A方面也有進展：洛克希德馬丁於2025年12月3日宣布，已在加州愛德華茲空軍基地完成地面振動測試與裝配檢查，僅剩一項地面測試即可開始搭載流星飛彈的飛行測試。英國主導F-35B的流星飛彈整合，義大利則負責F-35A；兩國皆操作F-35B。英國國防戰備與產業大臣盧克·波拉德於2026年4月20日的國會書面答覆中確認，流星飛彈在F-35B上形成作戰能力的預定時程仍指向2030年代初。
zh.summary: 洛克希德馬丁F-35B於10月7日在馬里蘭州帕圖森河海軍航空站首度自內置彈艙釋放MBDA流星飛彈測試體，驗證安全分離；英國預期2030年代初才能在F-35B上形成流星飛彈作戰能力。
zh.title: F-35B首度自內置彈艙釋放流星飛彈，邁向實彈試射
